about: What the Terraform in infra/aws is billed for in a 730-hour month in Seoul, with the line of Terraform that creates each item. Fixed items bill whether or not anything runs; usage items depend on the scenario inputs below, each with the assumption behind it. Prices come from the snapshot written by snapshot.py; estimate.py reads both offline, and estimate.py verify checks every citation and static quantity against the .tf files.
assumes: The variables keep their defaults: two Availability Zones, db_max_capacity 2, log_retention_days 400, alarm_emails empty. model_ids has no default, so no model is priced.

The account holds only this design, so every price tier starts at zero. The Price List's account-wide free tiers (separate Global SKUs) are listed, not subtracted; a $0 first tier inside a regional SKU is applied as published.
On-demand list prices in USD, before tax, credits, Savings Plans or reserved capacity.
Bytes are converted to GB as 2^30 bytes.

factors.what: Availability Zones, one app and one data subnet in each
Aurora Serverless v2 instances, one per Availability Zone
Minimum capacity of each instance, in ACUs
Days every log group keeps its records

fixed.what: Interface endpoints bedrock-runtime and logs, one network interface in each app subnet
fixed.derivation: 2 interface endpoints x 2 Availability Zones x 730 h

fixed.what: Aurora Serverless v2 at its minimum capacity, writer and reader
fixed.derivation: 2 instances x 0.5 ACU x 730 h. The reader sets no promotion tier, so it stays in tier 0 and follows the writer's capacity; both bill (Aurora user guide, How Aurora Serverless works). Performance Insights is off: the same guide recommends a minimum of 2 ACUs with it on, subject to change (Performance and scaling for Aurora Serverless), and turning it on at that minimum would make this line 2,920 ACU-Hr.

fixed.what: Customer managed KMS key (the lab key), rotation on
fixed.derivation: 1 key version in the first year. The SKU bills per key version; the KMS pricing page says the first and second yearly rotations each add one, so 2 in the second year and 3 from the third.

fixed.what: The database master password, kept by RDS in Secrets Manager
fixed.derivation: 1 secret; the Aurora user guide says secrets RDS keeps in Secrets Manager incur charges

fixed.what: Domain names stored in the two DNS Firewall domain lists
CloudWatch metric alarms, standard resolution, one metric each
fixed.derivation: Counted from the alarm resource blocks in the .tf files: a for_each map counts its keys, and count = length(aws_rds_cluster_instance.lab) counts the database instances. Each alarm watches one metric at a period of 60 s or more, which the count refuses otherwise. The SKU bills per alarm metric month.

fixed.what: SNS topic the alarms publish to, encrypted with the lab key
fixed.no_charge_reason: The Seoul AmazonSNS offer has no SKU for a standard topic; its publishes and email deliveries are priced per unit in the scenarios.

usage.what: Bedrock invocation log ingested, every body delivery off
Aurora PostgreSQL log exported (connections, disconnections, pgAudit DDL and role changes)
usage.note: Priced at the standard rate; whether the RDS export bills as vended logs was not checked. In Seoul both rates are 0.76 USD/GB below 10 TB a month.

usage.what: Log storage of the five groups once 400 days have filled
Data processed by the two interface endpoints
DNS queries inspected by DNS Firewall

usage.note: No storage_type is set, so the cluster uses Aurora Standard: storage and I/O are billed separately.

usage.what: Aurora backup storage beyond the free allocation
Aurora capacity above the minimum, both instances
KMS requests, alarm publishes to the encrypted topic included
Secrets Manager API requests (rotation of the master secret)
Alarm and recovery notifications published to the topic
Email deliveries, one per notification per subscribed address

usage.not_priced_reason: No model is chosen: model_ids has no default. The Price List names Seoul models by display name and usage type, with no attribute holding the Bedrock model ID that model_ids takes (see offers_checked_without_prices in the snapshot), and it does not say which models Seoul serves in-Region without a cross-Region inference profile, which the endpoint policy does not allow.
usage.formula: input_tokens / 1,000,000 x (USD per 1M input tokens of the chosen model)

usage.not_priced_reason: As for input tokens: no model is chosen and the Price List does not map to model IDs.
usage.formula: output_tokens / 1,000,000 x (USD per 1M output tokens of the chosen model)

usage.not_priced_reason: As for input tokens; which embedding models Seoul offers was not checked (infra/aws/README.md, Limits).
usage.formula: embedding_tokens / 1,000,000 x (USD per 1M input tokens of the chosen embedding model)

model_calls_per_run.basis: turns in evidence/rag-agent-20261022T082220Z-30c48f.json, one local agent run (qwen3:4b); a Bedrock model may take more or fewer turns, up to the 12-turn limit

embedding_calls_per_run.basis: one search_law call in that run's audit log; read_article reads the store without the model

input_tokens_per_call.basis: assumed at the 8,192-token context the lab gives RAG answers (rag/retrieval.py, num_ctx); prompt sizes were not measured

output_tokens_per_call.basis: the agents' 1,024-token response cap (agent/review_agent.py, num_predict), an upper bound

embedding_tokens_per_call.basis: the search argument in that run was 39 bytes; a token is at least one byte, so an upper bound

endpoint_bytes_per_call.basis: assumed: about 4 bytes per token at the token figures above plus request framing; not measured

agent_log_bytes_per_run.basis: the 12-line audit log of that run (evidence/rag-agent-20261022T082220Z-30c48f.jsonl)

invocation_log_bytes_per_call.basis: assumed; what a record holds with every body delivery off was not observed (infra/aws/README.md, Limits)

flow_log_bytes_per_run.basis: assumed: about 9 connections per run (model, embedding, logs, database), each recorded at both network interfaces in both directions, about 130 bytes per default-format record

dns_queries_per_run.basis: assumed: the agent looks up bedrock-runtime, logs and the cluster endpoint once per run

dns_log_bytes_per_query.basis: assumed size of one JSON query-log record; not measured

postgresql_log_bytes_per_run.basis: assumed: one connection per run, about three lines of about 200 bytes from log_connections and log_disconnections; Aurora's own connections are not counted

log_stored_fraction.basis: storage is billed on the compressed size, which was not measured; 1 (no compression) is an upper bound

kms_requests_per_publish.basis: one GenerateDataKey by CloudWatch and one Decrypt by SNS per notification to the encrypted topic; an upper bound, since data keys are reused

scenario_inputs.agent_runs: agent runs a month, each like the evidence run above
scenario_inputs.aurora_storage_gb: assumed: the corpus is 172 KB of text (rag/corpus/pipa.json) plus one 1,024-dimension vector per article; 1 GB leaves room for indexes, catalogs and WAL; not measured
scenario_inputs.aurora_io_requests: assumed; Aurora Standard bills each read and write I/O; not measured
scenario_inputs.aurora_average_acu_per_instance: assumed average capacity of each instance; never below the 0.5 minimum
scenario_inputs.aurora_backup_billed_gb: backup storage up to the cluster's size is not charged (Aurora pricing page); with 7 days' retention and a corpus that rarely changes, assumed to stay within it
scenario_inputs.kms_requests: assumed KMS calls of CloudWatch Logs, Aurora and Secrets Manager, not measured; the alarm publishes are added to this
scenario_inputs.secrets_api_requests: assumed: RDS rotates the master secret every seven days (Aurora user guide), a handful of calls each
scenario_inputs.alarm_notifications: assumed alarm state changes published to the topic; each alarm publishes again when it clears
scenario_inputs.alarm_email_addresses: alarm_emails is empty by default; addresses assumed per scenario

idle.about: Deployed and unused: no agent run, no alarm. A floor: Aurora's background I/O and connections and the KMS calls of log and database encryption were not measured and count as zero.

pilot.about: About ten people, each starting about ten agent runs a working day for 20 days; the database stays at its minimum.

busy.about: Ten times the pilot's runs, with each database instance averaging twice its minimum.

not_in_design: Compute for the agent (ECS tasks on Fargate or EC2): the Terraform has no cluster or task definition (infra/aws/README.md, Limits), so none is priced.
The ECR interface endpoints and S3 gateway endpoint that running tasks would need: not created, not priced. Two more interface endpoints would add 2 x 2 x 730 endpoint-hours.
Data transfer between Availability Zones: it depends on where the tasks run, which the design leaves open.
